newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST-HK NEWSPAPER EDITORIALS - AUG 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-HK NEWSPAPER EDITORIALS - AUG 7.

text.p: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL said China dare not learn from the good experience of other countries. It said no advanced country had succeeded economically without developing its political system at the same time, and no advanced country allowed political parties to interfere directly in the administration. The Journal asked how many of the "Chinese characteristics" that Beijing talked about were really good for the country's development.

-- WEN WEI PO said China was a developing country and it would be unfair and impractical to impose standards for advanced countries on China. It said opening up its service sector took time. It urged the World Trade Organisation to accept China as a member as soon as possible, because the WTO and China needed each other.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD said Chinese leaders were determined to push China towards economic modernisation and its rightful place in the world. It said they were following in the footsteps of late leader Deng Xiaoping, whose basic lesson essentially was that the ends justifies the means. It was a bold step forward, and the world was watching with bated breath, the paper said.
